items.followUp: Define the normal force and state when it acts.

rubric.why: Identifies where friction acts.
rubric.description: States that friction acts between surfaces in contact.
rubric.how: Award for identifying the contact between surfaces.

rubric.why: States the essential effect of friction.
rubric.description: Explains that friction opposes relative motion or its tendency.
rubric.how: Award for stating that friction opposes or resists motion.

modelAnswer: Friction is the force that opposes the relative motion, or the tendency of relative motion, between two surfaces in contact.

items.followUp: State two advantages of using solar energy.

rubric.why: Recognises electricity generation as a use of wind energy.
rubric.description: Gives electricity generation using wind turbines or windmills as one use.
rubric.how: Award for one valid use involving generating electricity.

rubric.why: Recognises another practical use of wind energy.
rubric.description: Gives a different valid use, such as pumping water, sailing boats, or grinding grain.
rubric.how: Award for a second distinct valid use.

modelAnswer: Wind energy is used to generate electricity with wind turbines.
It is also used to pump water.

items.followUp: Differentiate between elastic and inelastic bodies.

rubric.why: Describes the response of a body in stable equilibrium to a small displacement.
rubric.description: States that a slightly displaced body returns to its original position or has a restoring moment.
rubric.how: Award for the return or restoring effect.

rubric.why: Describes the response of a body in unstable equilibrium to a small displacement.
rubric.description: States that a slightly displaced body moves farther from its original position or has an overturning moment.
rubric.how: Award for the further-displacement or overturning effect.

modelAnswer: In stable equilibrium, a body returns to its original position when slightly displaced.
In unstable equilibrium, a body moves farther from its original position when slightly displaced.

items.followUp: State the first condition of equilibrium and explain what it ensures.

rubric.why: Identifies what the first condition of equilibrium establishes.
rubric.description: States that the first condition makes the resultant force zero.
rubric.how: Award for stating the zero-resultant-force condition.

rubric.why: Explains why the second condition is also needed.
rubric.description: States that the first condition does not ensure zero net torque, so the body could rotate; the second condition makes net torque zero.
rubric.how: Award for explaining the rotational limitation of the first condition and the need for zero net torque.

modelAnswer: The first condition, that the resultant force is zero, prevents translational acceleration.
It does not ensure that the net torque is zero, so the body may still rotate; the second condition is needed to ensure rotational equilibrium.

items.followUp: Name the fifth state of matter and briefly describe it.

rubric.why: Checks the name of the fourth state of matter.
rubric.description: Names plasma as the fourth state of matter.
rubric.how: Award for identifying plasma.

rubric.why: Checks the defining nature of plasma.
rubric.description: Defines plasma as an ionized gas containing charged particles such as ions and electrons.
rubric.how: Award for describing plasma as ionized or as a gas of charged particles.

modelAnswer: The fourth state of matter is plasma.
Plasma is an ionized gas made up of charged particles, such as ions and electrons.

items.followUp: What is a manometer used to measure?

rubric.why: Identifies a barometer as a measuring instrument.
rubric.description: States that a barometer is an instrument or device used for measurement.
rubric.how: Award for identifying it as a measuring instrument.

rubric.why: Checks the quantity measured by a barometer.
rubric.description: States that it measures atmospheric pressure.
rubric.how: Award for naming atmospheric or air pressure.

modelAnswer: A barometer is an instrument used to measure atmospheric pressure.

items.followUp: Using a speed-time graph, derive the equation v_f² = v_i² + 2as.

rubric.why: Checks that the graph is correctly represented and labelled.
rubric.description: Draws a speed-time graph with time on the horizontal axis, initial speed vᵢ at t = 0, and final speed v_f at time t.
rubric.how: Award for a correctly labelled graph showing the initial and final speeds over the time interval.

rubric.why: Uses the area under a speed-time graph to obtain displacement.
rubric.description: States that displacement is the area under the graph and writes S = vᵢt + 1/2(v_f − vᵢ)t.
rubric.how: Award for the area method and the rectangle-plus-triangle expression.

rubric.why: Uses the definition of acceleration to relate the change in speed to time.
rubric.description: Uses a = (v_f − vᵢ)/t, or equivalently v_f − vᵢ = at.
rubric.how: Award for the correct acceleration relation.

rubric.why: Checks the required derived equation.
rubric.description: Substitutes v_f − vᵢ = at into the area expression and obtains S = vᵢt + 1/2 at².
rubric.how: Award for the correct final equation.

modelAnswer: Draw a speed-time graph with time t on the horizontal axis and speed on the vertical axis.
Mark the speed at t = 0 as vᵢ and the speed at time t as v_f; join the points with a straight line for uniform acceleration.
Displacement S = area under the speed-time graph.
S = area of rectangle + area of triangle.
S = vᵢt + 1/2(v_f − vᵢ)t.
Acceleration a = (v_f − vᵢ)/t, so v_f − vᵢ = at.
Substituting, S = vᵢt + 1/2(at)t.
Therefore, S = vᵢt + 1/2at².

items.followUp: A 0.8 kg body moves in a circle of radius 0.4 m at 4 m s⁻¹. Calculate the centripetal force.

rubric.why: Checks that the given data are stated in SI units.
rubric.description: Lists m = 0.5 kg, r = 0.5 m (converted from 50 cm), and v = 3 m s⁻¹.
rubric.how: Award for the correct SI values, including conversion of the radius.

rubric.why: Checks selection of the centripetal-force formula.
rubric.description: Writes F_c = mv²/r.
rubric.how: Award for the correct formula.

rubric.why: Checks correct substitution and evaluation using the SI data.
rubric.description: Substitutes the values with units and evaluates the expression to 9.
rubric.how: Award for correct substitution and arithmetic; accept equivalent correctly evaluated working.

rubric.why: Checks the final force and its unit.
rubric.description: Gives the centripetal force as 9 N.
rubric.how: Award for the correct final answer with unit.

modelAnswer: Given: m = 0.5 kg, r = 50 cm = 0.5 m, v = 3 m s⁻¹.
Formula: F_c = mv²/r.
Substitution: F_c = (0.5 kg)(3 m s⁻¹)²/(0.5 m).
F_c = 4.5 kg m² s⁻² / 0.5 m = 9 kg m s⁻².
Therefore, the centripetal force required is 9 N.
